title: Longest Run of Ones With k Flips

concept.title: A window that may hold k bad elements
body: Flipping at most `k` zeros means: choose a block that contains **at most `k` zeros**; flipping those zeros turns the whole block into ones. So the question becomes the longest block with at most `k` zeros.

body.code:
zeros = l = best = 0
for r in range(n):
    if a[r] == 0: zeros += 1
    while zeros > k:
        if a[l] == 0: zeros -= 1
        l += 1
    best = max(best, r - l + 1)

body: This is the same shape as the previous windows: extend on the right, repair on the left, record the length. Only the "bad" thing being counted changes.

statement: You are given an array of 0s and 1s and a number `k`. You may change at most `k` zeros into ones. Print the length of the longest block of consecutive ones you can obtain.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers, each 0 or 1.

examples.note: Flip the zeros at indexes 2 and 3 (or 3 and 5): the longest block has length 5.

hints: Look for the longest block that has at most k zeros.
Count the zeros in the window; when there are more than k, move the left end.
Remember to reduce the count when the element that leaves is a zero.

explanation: The best result is the longest window containing at most `k` zeros: all its zeros can be flipped.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

zeros = 0
l = 0
best = 0
for rr in range(n):
    if a[rr] == 0:
        zeros += 1
    while zeros > k:
        if a[l] == 0:
            zeros -= 1
        l += 1
    best = max(best, rr - l + 1)
print(best)
